item.title: SF Schools Will Close if Teachers Strike. Here’s How City Hall Plans to Step In
item.description: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said city departments will offer free meals and some extended child care services on day one of a strike set for next week.

item.title: Sign Language Interpreter Will Also Make History During Super Bowl Halftime Show
item.description: For the first time, Puerto Rican Sign Language will be in the spotlight on one of the country’s biggest stages.

item.title: He’s Photographed Every Super Bowl. Will This One Be His Last?
item.description: When Super Bowl LX gets underway, there will be one photographer on the sidelines who has snapped shots at every Super Bowl game. John Biever was 15 when he took photos at the first Super Bowl; he says this one will likely be his last.

item.title: As Super Bowl Nears, Bay Area Braces for ICE Activity Despite Official Statements
item.description: Fears about a possible ICE presence in the Bay Area during the Super Bowl continue to simmer even as officials insist there are no planned enforcement operations tied to the game.

item.title: A Decade On, the Bay Area Is Hosting Another Super Bowl. How Have Prices Changed Since 2016?
item.description: 2016 was the last time the Bay Area hosted the Super Bowl. How much more expensive have things gotten since then?

item.title: This Stanford Student and Top US Speedskater Is Aiming for Gold at 2026 Winter Olympics
item.description: Brandon Kim, who’s been named one of the best skaters in the world, is competing for Team USA in short track speedskating.

item.title: San José’s Downtown Has Had a Strong Recovery. Is It Ready for the Super Bowl Surge?
item.description: For San José, the coming days are about more than just the big game; they’re a high-stakes test of downtown’s post-pandemic recovery.

item.title: Los Angeles Voters Are Moving Ever Leftward, Shifting Election Politics in America’s Second-Largest City
item.description: Once the bulwark of conservative politics in California, under the protection of a Republican business leadership and a Republican newspaper, LA has moved steadily leftward in recent decades.

item.title: California’s Instant Ev Rebates Would Require Automakers to Match State Funds
item.description: New budget language lays out how Gov. Gavin Newsom plans to structure a $200 million electric vehicle rebate program, including price caps, automaker matching funds and a focus on first-time buyers.

item.title: Bay Area Buzzes With Fans, Parties and Pageantry on Super Bowl Sunday
item.description: Tens of thousands of fans flooded Santa Clara and San Francisco for Super Bowl LX, turning streets around Levi’s Stadium into a lively fan festival filled with tailgate parties, team colors and anticipation for Bad Bunny’s halftime show.
